None of the ear rot references match -- they all show recognizable kernels with mold, not the complete replacement of ear contents with black spore masses seen in the test image.

My initial prediction is **Head_smut**. Let me check the confusion guide.

No confusion guide exists for Head_smut, so my prediction is not a known attractor.

The test image shows a corn ear where the normal kernel structure has been completely replaced by dark black spore masses, with the husks peeled back exposing the powdery/crumbly teliospores inside. This matches Head_smut perfectly -- the key distinguishing features are: (1) complete replacement of ear contents with black teliospores rather than fleshy galls (ruling out Common_smut), (2) no recognizable kernels remaining (ruling out all ear rots), and (3) the characteristic dried, fibrous vascular remnants visible within the spore mass.
